model_and_data: Gradient boosting based on symmetric decision trees, reformulated as a kernel method for regression. The located real-data experiments follow the setup of Malinin et al. (2021) and compare the proposed KGB with SGB, SGLB, and their ensembles on several standard regression datasets cited to Gal and Ghahramani (2016). Implementation details use the standard CatBoost library. Individual dataset names are not located in the quoted lines.
loss: RMSE. The extract says the analysis concerns regression problems assuming the widely used RMSE loss function, and that under this loss the gradients are proportional to the residuals. Logloss is absent from this extract.
held_fixed_axes: A double-descent complexity contrast with named axes held fixed was not located. The quoted analysis assumes the regularized gradient-boosting procedure, symmetric (oblivious) trees, proper randomization, RMSE loss, and shrinkage at each iteration.
assumptions: The theoretical target is regression under the RMSE loss.
The analysis assumes the regularized gradient-boosting procedure in Algorithm 2.
The quoted requirement is that decision trees be symmetric (oblivious) and properly randomized.
The extract says those assumptions are satisfied in some implementations, for example CatBoost.
Shrinkage of the model at each iteration is the regularization, and the extract says such shrinkage is available in CatBoost.
Under RMSE, gradients are proportional to residuals.
A footnote says any non-symmetric tree can be represented as a sum of symmetric ones. That sentence is about representation of the ensemble space.

Algorithm 2 is said to solve a kernel ridge regression problem interpreted as a Gaussian-process posterior mean. The scale relation is split across lines: one line ends at lambda = sigma2 and the next begins with delta2, with no division symbol on those lines, so the algebra is not repaired.
The same passage says Algorithm 2 does not give the posterior variance.
The implementation quote uses CatBoost and an L2 scoring function, and it prints a beta set whose exponent characters are left as extracted.
result_type: Theoretical equivalence, with regression experiments on predictive RMSE and uncertainty. Symmetric-tree gradient boosting with the stated regularization is carried to a kernel ridge solution and a Gaussian-process posterior mean. The extract says this algorithm does not itself provide the posterior variance. Double descent is absent from the extract.
transfer_limits: The kernel statement is tied to RMSE loss, shrinkage regularization, symmetric oblivious trees, and proper randomization. CatBoost is an example implementation and is used with the quoted L2 scoring function; logloss is absent. The footnote about writing a non-symmetric tree as a sum of symmetric trees does not extend the result to a double-descent axis comparison. The split lambda and delta2 line is ambiguous and is not repaired. This extract is context for those kernel assumptions and is not evidence that the tree experiments in L05, L06, and L07 vary the same axis.
